title: Top Agentic AI Companies in 2026
summary: The top agentic AI companies in 2026, from frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic to enterprise platforms and vertical specialists like Concourse.
body_markdown:
The agentic AI landscape got crowded fast. In the space of two years, "AI company" went from meaning a model lab to spanning frontier labs, the big enterprise software vendors, a wave of well-funded startups, and vertical specialists building agents for one industry. Sorting out who does what, and who actually builds agentic AI versus bolts a chatbot onto an existing product, is the point of this guide.


Here are the top agentic AI companies in 2026, grouped by the layer they operate at, with what each builds and the latest funding where it is public. For the concept behind it all, see our guide to[agentic AI](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/agentic-ai) ; for the products, see[best agentic AI tools](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/agentic-ai-tools) .


## **The layers of the agentic AI landscape**


The companies worth knowing fall into three groups:


- **Frontier model labs** build the models that do the reasoning, and increasingly their own agent platforms: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind.
- **Enterprise platforms** embed agents into the software companies already run: Microsoft, Salesforce, and other incumbents.
- **Agent-native startups and vertical specialists** build agents as the product, horizontally (Sierra, Cognition) or for one industry (Concourse for finance).


## **Frontier model labs**


### **OpenAI**


OpenAI is the most prominent AI company, with consumer agents (ChatGPT agent mode) and a full developer stack for building agents. Private and, per 2025 reporting, valued around $500 billion in a secondary share sale, it is the most valuable private company in the world, and the default platform much of the agent ecosystem builds on.


### **Anthropic**


Anthropic builds the Claude model family, a leader for agentic coding and computer use, plus the Claude Agent SDK. It[raised a $13B Series F at a $183B post-money valuation in September 2025](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-raises-series-f-at-usd183b-post-money-valuation) . It is OpenAI's closest rival at the frontier.


### **Google DeepMind**


Google DeepMind, Alphabet's unified AI division (formed by merging DeepMind and Google Brain in 2023), builds the Gemini models and Google's enterprise agent stack on Vertex AI. Part of Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL), it pairs frontier research with Google Cloud's distribution.


## **Enterprise platforms**


### **Microsoft**


Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) brings agents to the enterprise through Copilot Studio (autonomous agents across Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365) and the open-source Microsoft Agent Framework for developers. Combined with its OpenAI partnership and distribution, it is one of the most important agentic AI companies for enterprises.


### **Salesforce**


Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) bet heavily on agents with Agentforce, its "digital labor" platform of autonomous agents for service, sales, and marketing embedded in the Salesforce stack. It is among the most aggressive incumbents in positioning agents as the next platform shift.


## **Agent-native startups and vertical specialists**


### **Sierra**


Sierra, founded by Bret Taylor (former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair) and Clay Bavor, builds autonomous customer-service agents and is one of the highest-profile agent startups. It[raised $350M at a $10B valuation in September 2025](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/04/bret-taylors-sierra-raises-350m-at-a-10b-valuation/) .


### **Cognition (Devin)**


Cognition builds Devin, the autonomous AI software engineer, and owns the Windsurf agentic IDE after acquiring it in 2025. Private and, per reporting, valued around $10.2 billion in September 2025, it is a leader in agentic software development.


### **Concourse, the finance specialist**


Concourse is the vertical agentic AI company for corporate finance. Rather than a general platform, it builds AI agents that connect to a company's ERP, data warehouse, and banking data and run finance workflows, forecasting, variance analysis, reconciliations, and reporting, end to end, with every output traceable to source and a human approving. It is SOC 2 Type II certified, connects to 100+ systems, and customers report cutting manual work by roughly 75%.


> The broad labs and platforms build the horizontal capability; the vertical specialists make it usable and trustworthy in one domain. In finance, that means agents that not only do the work but tie every number back to source, so it holds up to a board and an auditor.


## **A note on the hype**


Two cautions when reading any "top agentic AI companies" list. First, most such lists are published by vendors ranking themselves, so weigh the source. Second, many companies now market "AI agents" for what is really a chatbot or a workflow with a model attached, true agentic AI plans, uses tools, and takes action autonomously. The test is whether the product does the work or just talks about it. One well-known cautionary tale: Adept, an early agent startup, was effectively absorbed into Amazon via an acqui-hire in 2024 rather than becoming a standalone leader.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What are the top agentic AI companies?**


At the frontier: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind. Among enterprise platforms: Microsoft and Salesforce. Among agent-native and vertical specialists: Sierra (customer service), Cognition/Devin (software engineering), and Concourse (finance). The landscape spans model labs, enterprise incumbents, and specialists building agents for specific jobs.


### **Which company is the leader in agentic AI?**


There is no single leader, it depends on the layer. OpenAI and Anthropic lead at the model and capability layer, Microsoft and Salesforce at embedding agents in enterprise software, and vertical specialists lead within their domains. Most organizations end up using several together.


### **Are there agentic AI companies focused on finance?**


Yes. Concourse is a vertical agentic AI company built for corporate finance, deploying agents that run finance workflows end to end with audit-ready traceability. Vertical focus matters in finance because the work requires domain knowledge and every output has to be defensible to leadership and auditors.


## **The bottom line**


The top agentic AI companies span three layers: frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind) building the models, enterprise platforms (Microsoft, Salesforce) embedding agents in existing software, and specialists (Sierra, Cognition, Concourse) building agents to do a specific job. The horizontal players supply the capability; the vertical ones make it trustworthy in a domain.
